text:
Priya (CS): Flagging Seabright onboarding: their p95 is creeping up (from ~280ms -> ~610ms) and token spend is trending +28% month-over-month. Renewal in 6 weeks. Recommend a proactive compact-model trial + routing hedge before renewal convo. Thoughts?

Daniel (Solutions): Do we know if the prompt distribution shifted? Long conversations or lots of short calls?

Priya (CS): Ops notes show more multi-turn flows and a new template that includes a 400-token system prompt. Average prompt_tokens bumped from 150 -> 370.

Omar (SRE): Two possible levers: 1) swap to rw-compact-1-int4 for short/medium prompts, 2) route long (>500 tokens) to rw-base-3b. Also enable per-customer prefix cache (TTL 60s) for repeated opening messages.

Priya (CS): Customer-facing line I'd propose: "We can reduce latency and monthly inference cost by ~18-30% with a targeted compact-model canary and smart routing. We'll monitor quality and only proceed if we meet your accuracy guardrails."

Daniel (Solutions): Agree. I'll run a quick A/B on their goldenset (n=800). Acceptance criteria: intent match >=98% of baseline and semantic similarity drop <1.5% (BLEU/SBERT heuristic).

Omar (SRE): Instrumentation checklist: add ab_label=seabright_compact_trial, token_diff logging, and an alert if p95 increases >12% or error_rate >1.0%. Also snapshot latency by prompt_length bucket.

Priya (CS): Draft routing + cache snippet for Console copy: 

```
routing_rules:
  - condition: prompt_tokens > 500
    route: rw-base-3b
  - condition: prompt_tokens <= 500
    route: rw-compact-1-int4  # canary 15%
cache:
  prefix_kv: enabled
  ttl_seconds: 60
monitoring:
  ab_label: seabright_compact_trial
  golden_set: seabright_onboard_800
```

metricsbot: [metric-alert] baseline_p95: 280 -> current_p95: 610 (48h window)

Daniel (Solutions): Plan: 15% traffic canary for 24h -> evaluate quality/latency/cost -> 50% for 24h if green -> full. Automated rollback triggers: quality delta >1.5% or p95 regression >12% vs baseline.

Priya (CS): I'll ask Seabright for sign-off and schedule a 30m enablement to walk through the tradeoffs. I'll also offer to include an estimated monthly savings figure for their renewal packet.

Omar (SRE): Heads-up: int4 quant is more aggressive than int8; it gives bigger savings but higher risk of distributional shift. We should run a logits-drift check and include a small manual QA pass on 50 high-risk prompts (long-context).

Daniel (Solutions): Good call. I'll include a quick manual pass in the evaluation run. If manual QA flags >3 failures, we'll abort.

Priya (CS): Thanks — marking this thread as the source of truth for Seabright compact trial. Will post the customer's go/no-go and the evaluation results here. :wave:
